MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 14, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:00 p.m., on May 14, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 9, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation; Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 2 cases.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  May 14, 2019
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed three matters in Closed Session.
The Council received updates and gave direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Mission Viejo High School Boys Volleyball Team as Seaview League
  Champions

  Mayor Raths presented certificates of recognition to the players and coaches of the Mission
  Viejo High School Boys Volleyball Team.

P2. Proclaim the Month of May 2019 as be Mental Health Awareness Month

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Yeslee Fuentes, Lead Outreach and Engagement
  Specialist for Western Youth Services.

P3. Featured Business of the Month - A-Z Tech Automotive

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to the owner of A-Z Tech Automotive, Amir
  Mohammadpour.

P4. Key to the City - VIDA Dentistry

  Mayor Raths presented Dr. Jocelynn Vida Sustaita with a Key to the City.

P5. I-5 Widening Project

  The City Council received an update on the I-5 widening project from Niall Barrett, Program
  Manager for Orange County Transportation Authority.

P6. State Legislative Update

  The City Council received the legislative update from Cori Williams with Townsend Public
  Affairs.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Julianne Tawara and Delaney Adan, M.V.: announced that their team, Jiggly Jumpin’ Jittery
Jellybeans, are competing in the Destination Imagination competition and they are seeking
financial support from the community.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the public record didn't contain a redlined version of the
Municipal Code changes for agenda item 2. She expressed concern that the City Council will no
City Council Minutes  2  May 14, 2019
 longer have the approval authority for use of the City’s recreational facilities in Section 13.020.050
of the Code.

Grace Belletti, M.V.: expressed concern with the size of trees that were recently planted near her
home and the potential that the trees will block her views as they grow.

Nikki Wattf, M.V.: stated that her neighbor is operating an Airbnb and it is causing traffic
problems, trash, noise and other isssues.

Sharon Siqueiros, M.V.: expressed concern with activities that result from the Airbnb rental unit
next door to her home. She said her grandson's bedroom overlooks the patio and pool and there is
trash everywhere plus people drinking, smoking, and making noise until 2:00 a.m.

Wilson Encarnacino, M.V.: announced that he has launched a new business called Crooru which
is like Uber for healthcare staffing. He noted that there will be a Senior Caregiver Appreciation
Day celebration at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center on June 15, 2019, from
11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. and he invited the senior caregiving community to participate.

Michael Rochter, M.V.: reminded the Council and residents of an upcoming Community Choice
Energy Seminar on June 21 in Irvine. He said it will be a great opportunity for people to learn, ask
questions and network with other cities.

Ron Yee, Chairman of the Mission Viejo Community of Character Committee, M.V.: announced
that the character word for the month of May is moral courage.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to authorize

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

36. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including a Donate Life
awareness event, Family Arts Day at Potocki Center for the Arts, sponsored by the Kiwanis Club,
and the Mayor's Prayer Breakfast. She also attended the Association of California Cities-Orange
County luncheon and was honored to present City Manager Dennis Wilberg with ACC-OC’s City
Manager of the Year award. Council Member Bucknum said that she and her husband, Paul,
participated in the Sheriff Department’s Citizens Academy and they found it very informative.
She also attended the meeting that Council Member Sachs organized for Secure OC Schools. She
said she was impressed to see so many churches and schools represented and there were attendees
from as far north as Yorba Linda. Council Member Bucknum noted that the word is spreading and
it's a good concerted effort with Mission Viejo at the lead in school safety efforts.

City Council Minutes  9  May 14, 2019
 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley extended congratulations to Dennis Wilberg on his City Manager of the
Year award. She said that residents need to know that the City has an extremely talented and
exceptional City Manager and he is one of the reasons Mission Viejo has done so well as a
community. Council Member Kelley noted that Verizon has been installing fiber optic cable in
preparation for 5G and for those people who have asked if the damaged roads will be repaired, the
answer is yes. She encouraged residents to stop by and see the American Heroes Tribute Banners
on display outside of city hall and to mark their calendars for the City’s Memorial Day ceremony
on May 27 at 8:30 a.m. at City Hall. She also recommended El Toro Cemetery’s Memorial Day
event at 11:00 a.m. where Mayor Raths will be the keynote speaker. Council Member Kelley
announced that the City is hiring lifeguards and offering certification classes which is a great
opportunity for summer jobs. She further shared that in Orange County, residents can now text
911 in an emergency if they cannot call. The first text should be brief and include the location and
a request for police, fire or an ambulance. She reminded the community of the Marine Adoption
Committee’s Boots, Beer & BBQ event s which is a fundraiser for the City’s adopted Marines.
Tickets are $25 per person and can be purchased at the Murray Community Center or online at
mvcommunityfoundation.org. Council Member Kelley announced that the City has again won a
national award for its character program and she shared that the character word for the month of
May is moral courage. The character movie, I am Sam, will be shown in the Council Chamber on
Sunday, May 19 at 2:00 p.m.

Council Member Sachs

Referring to the OCTA presentation earlier in the meeting, Council Member Sachs expressed
concern about the effect of the I-5 widening project on the City’s intersections. He said he recently
drove through the City of Seal Beach where a freeway widening is taking place and the detours
were incredible. He believes that the I-5 widening project is going to be a mess and residents
should plan to leave for their destinations very early. He also thanked Council Member Bucknum
for bringing up the May 1 Secure OC Schools event and said that the goal is to create a platform
for early warning to first responders and a communications app that can be used during an event
at any public facility. Council Member Sachs announced that the name of the organization has
been changed to “Secure Our Communities” and he noted that every school in Mission Viejo will
be given the communications app at no charge and every Catholic school in the County of Los
Angeles will soon be using it. He shared that at a recent school exercise, the apps designer turned
a 45-minute active shooter drill into a 10-minute drill due to the efficiency of the platform. In
closing, Council Member Sachs congratulated Dennis Wilberg and said he wished he could have
attended the event to honor him for his City Manager of the Year award.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell also congratulated City Manager Wilberg on his award and he agreed
that the Secure our Communities partnership is an amazing program and he cannot wait for
residents to learn about it. The smartphone app will connect schools, first responders, churches
and governments and they are also providing Stop the Bleed Kits at all Mission Viejo schools.
Mayor Pro Tem Goodell stated that it is a very important program and training is going to be very
valuable towards its success. He offered his congratulations to Council Member Sachs and the
team for putting such a great idea into play. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell noted that he and his wife
attended the Sheriff Department’s Citizens academy and learned a lot about the professionalism
City Council Minutes  10  May 14, 2019
 and resources that the City’s officers have available to protect the community. He also discussed
the dirt that will be available to the City as a result of the I-5 widening project and shared that he
hopes the City can create new parklands where there are currently hillsides.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths congratulated the Rotary Club for putting on an amazing Mayor's Prayer Breakfast
and he thanked Paul Bucknum for doing a fantastic job leading the event. He announced that the
Chamber of Commerce is hosting its next mixer at Jacuzzi Outdoor Living at 5:30 p.m. on
Thursday, May 16. Mayor Raths stated that the country has said goodbye to two great Americans,
Doris Day and Tim Conway, and he announced that the meeting will be closed in memory of
Kendrick Castillo, the young hero from Colorado who died protecting his classmates during a live
shooter attack at his high school.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:34 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting, in memory of Kendrick Castillo, to Tuesday, May 28, 2019,
at 5:00 p.m.
